steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.

Grease a large (9x13) casserole dish. Place a quarter of the macaroni in the bottom, followed by an even layer of one-quarter of the cheese slices. Dot with butter and season with salt and pepper. Repeat layering three times. Pour evaporated milk evenly over the top of all.
Bake in preheated oven, uncovered, until cheese melts and top is golden brown, 40-60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Macaroni and Cheese
raw_recipe.description: Elbow macaroni is layered with Cheddar cheese and baked with evaporated milk in this easy classic.

review.reviewBody: I thought this was great, but I made some changes. Reduced cooking temp to 350, used 12oz of noodles instead of a pound, used half mild cheddar and half Kraft Deluxe American Cheese (sandwich slices), and increased the amount of evaporated milk. This was a homerun for all three kids and it reminded me of the way it used to taste when I was growing up.

I am giving this 4 stars because the cooking temp and ingredient ratios are off for our taste. We like more cheese and milk. I love, love, love the fact that you don't make a cheese sauce to poor over the noodles before baking. I remember my mother making this dish without making a separate sauce. I have made this about 5 times now. I use 1lb of cubed cheese and 1lb of shredded cheese. The type of cheese varies depending on what I have on hand. I mix the cheeses and macaroni in a 9x14 glass dish, then I beat a couple of eggs, 3 cups of milk, garlic, and pepper (no salt) to pour over the mixture and bake covered with aluminum foil for 1 hour. Our preference is to also add a topping of breadcrumbs or crushed crackers with a little melted butter and bake another 15 minutes. I encourage you to play with the ratios until you get it just the way your family loves it.

To fill a 2½-quart casserole dish or a 9x9 baking pan, I suggest using 8 oz. of small elbows (2 cups), not 1 lb., plus 8 oz. of cheddar (which you grate/shred yourself) & a 12 oz. can of evap. milk. But whisk into the milk 1 tsp. paprika, ½ tsp. of mustard powder, & ¼ tsp. each of ground black pepper, red pepper (cayenne) & garlic powder. Before grating the cheddar into the cooked elbows, stir 8 oz. of whipped cream cheese into them (for richness & to prevent clumping of the cheddar). The heat of the elbows will start melting the cream cheese. Then add the seasoned milk & stir until the cream cheese is completely melted. Next, grate/shred the cheddar into the mix, stirring as you go. It'll melt in the oven. Suggested extras: 2 hot dogs sliced into coins; 1 cup of frozen baby peas, 1/3 cup each of diced scallions & green pepper (or 1/4 cup of diced jalapenos!). Bake at 350 for ½ hr., covered; then 325 for ½ hr., uncovered. BTW, a 2-qt. dish or 8x8 pan will be too small for this.

This recipe is a great template, but I made lots of changes other reviewers suggested and it turned out great! I used 12 oz macaroni, 8 oz lowfat shredded Italian-blend cheese, about 10 oz shredded sharp cheddar cheese, and about 18 oz fat-free evaporated milk. Instead of layering the butter, I mixed in about 2 T light butter to the cooked macaroni. In a medium bowl, I mixed the cheeses together, and added to that a mix of dry mustard, garlic salt, paprika, salt, and white pepper. I made it in 4 layers, as the recipe calls for. I baked it in a 3-quart casserole at 350F, covered for the first 30 minutes, then uncovered for the last 35 minutes. (Next time I will cook it covered for less time to get a better baked crust. You can see my result in my photo.) Everyone but my 3-year old loved it; he expected the stuff from the box. I'll definitely make this again!

I made this but I did it at 350 for around 45min and covered it also after every layer of macaroni and cheese I put a little bit of butter and at the end I put half a cup of Italian bread crumbs then poured the evaporated milk over it.

I have made this every year for the past several years for special occasions, holidays, and company potlucks. It's a true custard style Mac & cheese recipe. For people that grew up on this style, it's the best. I do add mustard powder, onion powder, garlic powder, and Italian bread crumbs dotted with butter on top. This just adds a little more flavor and a breaded topping. I also use a large oval 7 quart slow cooker & double the recipe. When I bring it to work, I plug it in there and cook on low for 3 hours. By the time it's ready, it's hot and good to go. I get many complements and requests for this at work & home. It's never been a disappointment.

My family loved this. I used an additional 6 oz. can of evaporated milk, and also reduced the temperature to 350 degrees. Using the recommendation of Kraft Deluxe slices and mild cheddar made this a great dish!

Great with modifications: used half mild cheddar and half colby, cut into cubes, replaced evap milk with 8 oz. of sour cream, added two eggs, and sprinkled about two handfuls of shredded colby/monterey jack on top, during the last 10 minutes. Last, but not least, lowered the temp to 350.

Very nice recipe for a juicy mac&cheese.

Followed the comments and baked 40 mins on 180• but the last 20 turned on 200 degrees.
I've made my own evaporated milk by reducing full fat milk on a very low heat until its size was twice reduced and I may say the result was fabulous.
Also, made only two layers since my ikea dish was very small ;)) my husband is normally very picky but this time had nooo comments at all ;)) Bon appetite and thank you for the nice dinner!

Made it tonight and it was my first time ever, making homemade mac and cheese. Everyone loved it! I made a 9x12 pan and doubled the recipe, I also used Kraft Deluxe American cheese and shredded mild cheddar cheese. I melted my butter and mixed in ground mustard, white pepper and salt. Mixed that in with the pasta, then layered it with the cheese. I poured over two cans of evaporated milk and covered it with foil. I baked it on 350 for about 45 minutes. Will definitely be making this again and again!

I made a few changes using some of the previous suggestions. I used 2 cups shredded mild cheddar and 2 cups shredded casserole blend (cheddar, american, monterey jack and mozzarella cheeses). Instead of evaporated milk, I used 3 cups 1% milk. I baked at 375 degrees for 30 minutes. I took my macaroni and cheese to a cookout and it was a big hit. Everyone went back for seconds and the bowl came home empty. I had many requests for copy of the recipe.
Good for kids. Very quick and easy.
I made this for Thanksgiving dinner and it was quite the disappointment! Made as written … wish I’d have made it before thanksgiving!

I made so many changes, I basically came up with a new recipe, but I definitely based it on this. Double the cheese, and make half of it American. Forget the butter. Forget the salt. Forget the pepper. Forget dotting. Pour drained noodles back into the pot. Add 2 ounces of lard, one packet of dry onion soup mix, and the evaporated milk. Stir thoroughly; layer as directed above. Bake at 350°F, covered, for 45 minutes. Remove foil. Continue to bake until desired brownness is reached, at least 15 minutes.
